title: Do HTTP Features Carry the Signal? Shortcut Learning and Label Errors inWeb Attack Detection on CIC-IDS2017 and CSIC 2010
content: Intrusion detection studies often report very high scores on the CIC-IDS2017 benchmark and credit new feature sets with the gain. We reassess a representative design, a deep neural network over 21 flow statistics and 10 HTTP aware features taken from the SentinelSphere platform, under a protocol that controls for known pitfalls, and we retest the features on the CSIC 2010 dataset, which contains real HTTP requests. On the flow based CIC-IDS2017 data the ten HTTP features are identically zero, because flow records contain none of the request fields they read, and the 64 by 64 network as described reaches only 6\% recall at the conventional threshold, finding none of the 21 SQL injection flows. Tree ensembles do exceed a 94\% F1 score, but a depth three tree on a single flow metadata feature, the backward initial TCP window size, already reaches an area under the curve of 0.985, so much of the apparent skill is a dataset artefact. The corrected labels of the same traffic show that only 104 of 2,056 web attack flows are successful attacks, and catching those is harder. On real requests the ten features reach an F1 of about 0.91 once the body is included and decoded, a plain character ngram model reaches 0.97, and an ablation traces the signal to a generic path entropy feature rather than to the attack pattern flags.
